I'm a junior admin at a small business. I have a boss who wants to implement RAID 1 on all workstations. A period of time ago, we had a bunch of disk failures that convinced him that this was necessary. I have advised against this due to the hardware costs and the fact that most drives nowadays are stable and don't fail often (we are using HDDs still instead of SSDs)

From my understanding of RAID 1, if a drive fails, you plug in a new one and the RAID controller automatically starts replicating from the good drive to the new drive.

He also seems to think that if you have RAID 1 in place on a workstation, that if a drive fails, Windows 7/10 will automatically switch over to using the spare drive, while you go procure a new one to replace the failed drive - thereby losing no uptime on the workstation.

I've never heard of that second one. Can someone confirm?

We are using the Intel RAID controller on the motherboard, not a standalone hardware controller.

Ive seen this:

1) 3Ware raid cards - power down system, replace drive, enter raid card firmware, rebuild

2) Windows - who knows, you had better test this thoroughly yourself before mass deployment

Honestly, drive failures are fairly rare for workstations. Why not just store any sensitive information centrally and back it up from there? If it's a productivity issue, keep a spare workstation to deploy in the event of a failure. I'm also not sure that RAID1 can do a live rebuild or not. Performance would be god-awful if so. RAID5 (if drives are smaller than 1TB) or RAID6 might meet the requirement for live rebuild better, but the costs are way higher.

Completely agree that it's a bad idea, I'm trying to convince him of this, but I need to confirm that the second scenario isn't a thing before I can go to him. Googling hasn't really helped, I can't find a definitive answer one way or another so I was trying to grab first-hand knowledge from some of the admins here.
Windows has built in mirroring via disk manager and it actually works very well. For RAID 1 you don't really benefit performance wise by using a hardware controller anyway.
